pos.personaBrief: Bola na Rede: Chelsea is not a team that wants the ball, with a low 5-4-1 block and wing-back counters; 13 straight wins and 81 non-penalty goals came without possession dominance.

pro.personaBrief: Safe, direct style: Kante and Matic protect the back three, Luiz plays long balls, and wing-backs get the fast progression; Spurs' press forced Chelsea long.

est.personaBrief: Conte gives rigid individual roles (Scroll) in a defined 3-4-3 / 5-4-1; wing-backs hold the flank while Hazard and Pedro drift inside.

lar.personaBrief: Attack comes through high wing-backs Alonso and Moses with Hazard and Pedro inside, though few crosses were played (StatsBomb).

blo.personaBrief: Low block 5-4-1, no aggressive reaction to loss, fewer than 10 shots conceded in a 12-match run (Bola na Rede, StatsBomb).

mar.personaBrief: Zonal defending by ball position (Bola na Rede); Hazard was man-marked by opponents, not by Chelsea.

pla.personaBrief: Conte imposed his system and adapted it to the squad (plan D, 3-4-3 after Arsenal), changing at half-time when losing; drilled model over opponent study.

res.personaBrief: Pragmatic: switched to a five-man midfield to close games, 'the pitch is the truth', a title built on solidity and results.

sis.personaBrief: Rigid roles, Hazard freed from defending only because the system protects him; Conte said the best player does not exist without a team and he prefers to lose over selfishness.

jog.personaBrief: Work rate: Chelsea out-ran United by 8.54km, Kante and Moses and Alonso engine; Luiz and Costa physical.

bas.personaBrief: Built through purchases (Alonso, Luiz, Kante) and veterans like Cahill and Costa; no academy focus.

lid.personaBrief: Meticulous, equal treatment, no favouritism, coach has the last word (Irish Times, Scroll).
